findings.text: General slab object release accepts a cache and an object pointer, resolves owning slab metadata from the address, optionally validates the association when hardening or consistency checking is active and leaks rather than proceeds on mismatch, then hands off to the common free path.

Central free routine applies group and tagging adjustments first, then runs a per object veto that can consume the free, then attempts fast per CPU placement and only on failure takes the slow shared path while counting slow events.

Address to slab translation goes through page lookup with compound coalescing followed by a slab type test that yields absence for non slab pages; slab to folio and base address conversions are identity views of the same storage.
Debug flag queries are meaningful only when the debug facility is compiled and dynamically enabled; otherwise they report inactive, and one build variant always reports inactive.

Initialization on free follows a system default branch with per cache exclusions for constructors, type safe reclamation and poisoning; when the default branch is off no cache requests initialization.

Leak detector object destruction runs after references reach zero without locking, detaches and releases every registered scan area, then returns the object either to a reserved pool free list or to its cache depending on address range.
Reserved pool free list updates are protected by a raw spin lock held with interrupts saved; objects outside the pool bypass locking entirely.

Per object extension storage is retrieved as a masked pointer with flag bits removed, with one build variant always reporting absence; access is bracketed by metadata guards that suspend sanitizer tracking.

Extension record location derives from object offset within the slab scaled by object size and a stride that differs between embedded and external storage; total record size accounts independently for group and tagging needs, with per slab and per cache variants for group need and placement.
Tag reference lookup assumes tagging support is present and skips a leading group record when group accounting is active; tagging presence is controlled by a build dependent branch.

Allocation tagging on free is inactive unless profiling is enabled and the cache permits extensions and tracing; otherwise it reduces the per object tag by the cache size for each object in the batch.

Group aware free is skipped when kernel memory accounting is offline, when the slab has no extension storage, or when the slab needs no group records; otherwise each object detaches its group reference, updates batched stock accounting, and releases the reference.
Per CPU charge stock uses a local try lock that may fail; failure yields a null handle that forces direct unbatched accounting, and release is a no operation for null.

Byte level slab statistics are batched per cached group and node; identity change flushes pending reclaimable and unreclaimable deltas, small combined deltas stay cached while large ones flush directly, and cache misses bypass batching.

Slab statistic updates go through group to node vector adjustment with dying group redirection; one variant uses atomic per node counters in non maskable context and vector updates otherwise, while another always uses the vector path.

Statistic flushing is governed by per CPU update counters aggregated to shared totals once a batch threshold is crossed unless already flushable; byte values convert to page units with rounding up of sub page remainders using per item units.

Vector updates target the nearest non dying ancestor when the default hierarchy is not in use, holding read side protection across the walk; default hierarchy and simplified builds use the supplied group directly without protection.

Object charge bytes accumulate in small per CPU slots indexed by group; slot miss reuses an empty slot or evicts a rotating victim after draining, full pages are uncharged while sub page remainders stay cached, and slot absence charges bytes directly to the group counter.

Hierarchical counters propagate charges and releases through all ancestors, maintain peak watermarks with local and global levels, distribute protected usage for minimum and low thresholds to parents, and clamp accidental negative usage to zero with a one time warning.

Releasing a pointer whose slab lookup fails or whose owning cache mismatches triggers a diagnostic and intentional leak instead of freeing; statistics updates are intentionally racy and bad statistic indexes trigger diagnostics.

Slab metadata aliases folio storage so the same address serves both views; extension records pack an optional group reference followed by an optional tag reference with dynamic sizing; pool objects link through a reused list node for free management.

Statistic index validity is bounded by an eight bit maximum; node count is constrained below signed sixteen bit maximum for stock storage; stock deltas use sixteen bit signed caching with page size flush threshold and fixed batch aggregation.

Per CPU byte stock cycles between unbound, bound to a group and node with pending deltas, and flushed; identity change or threshold breach forces a flush transition before rebinding, while direct mode bypasses the bound state.
